Home / Our story

Three generations,
one charcoal grill

Yang's Smokehouse is a family business that started with one widow, one charcoal stall and a spice blend she never wrote down.

传承

How it started

At thirty, facing the sudden loss of her husband, Grandma Yang didn't just survive. She commanded the embers.

  1. 1980

    A charcoal stall in Guiyang

    With five children to raise, she opened a single skewer stall in the capital of Guizhou province, seasoning everything with spices she crushed by hand.

  2. Six stalls, ten thousand skewers a day

    Word spread. The family grew the business to six locations, each grilling around 10,000 skewers a day.

  3. Forty years at the fire

    Grandma Yang ran her grills for four decades, then handed the recipes to her youngest daughter.

  4. A third generation in Texas

    Her granddaughter Candice Cao came to Dallas more than a decade ago to study at Dallas Baptist University. Together with her mother, she brought the family recipes to Plano.

  5. Grandma flies in

    Grandma Yang traveled to Texas to help open Yang's Smokehouse and coach the kitchen team herself.

  6. 2026

    “Sensational skewers”

    CultureMap Dallas featured the restaurant, singling out the lamb, beef tongue and crispy tofu balls. Read the article

Two vows

The rules Grandma Yang set at the first stall still run our kitchen.

一

Honest meat

Quality cuts, marinated properly and grilled to order. If it isn't good enough for the family table, it doesn't go on a skewer.

二

The blend stays secret

Grandma Yang's chili and spice mix is still crushed by hand from a recipe that has never been written down. You can take a jar home as Soul Chili Powder.

BBQ, reimagined in Plano

Every skewer is marinated in our 40-year signature spice tradition before it meets live fire. Grab a seat where you can watch the grill: the smoke is half the experience.

We pair the classics with dishes from home, like crispy tofu balls, Kaili sour soup fish and the crispy pork crunch rice bowl, and with a few Texas touches, like skewer-meat tacos.
